posts.author: JohnDoeGames
posts.body:
You can open the database (F9), go to tilesets, and create a new tileset.
Now you can pick the sheets you want to use in that set, and you you have a new set.

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
when making a new tileset, please keep in mind that there are six different formats of tilesheets.
slot A1 can only take tilesheets formatted as A1, slot A2 can only take tilesheets formatted as A2 and so on.
only B-E use the same format and can be interchanged.
however you can use an image program to replace unused tiles with tiles from other tilesheets as long as you keep the formats.

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
japanfreak said:
i don't see the point why i can't i use all of them on the same map
Click to expand...
you need to store the tiles, which is done by storing numbers.
and the space available for storing numbers in the map structure is limited - which means it can only use a limited number of tiles.
like a single byte on the computer can only store the numbers 0 to 255, you cannot store a number higher than 255 in a single byte.
Map storage is a bit more complex than that, but still limited - and the current tileset limits go to the maximum allowed in the current map storage structure.
To change that would require a complete rework of the map structure - which would also break compatibility to older makers and remove the option to use their resources as easily as it is now possible.

posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
japanfreak said:
i understand from a keeping everything organized it makes sense you have outside and inside dungeon etc but i don't see the point why i can't i use all of them on the same map
Click to expand...
Because one of the points of dividing the game into different maps is to separate by area type, and because the tilesheet has a specific format with finite space on it.
If it were infinitely expandable and people could just dump as much in one sheet as they worked, it would take increasing amounts of time and RAM to load the sheet and your game wouldn't run on some people's computers (or potentially any).
You may be better off learning how to make parallax maps, if you feel you can't work with the included map tile system. But there are no games that just have all resources dumped into any given map. Even newer 3D games aren't tile-based as such, but they load only the specific textures that they need for an area.

If i may give a word of advice : if you think about giving up already, it's definitely not a mindset that will lead you to finish a project.
You WILL stumble upon massive roadblocks during dev.
99,9% of the time, they have a solution. Don't give up, find the solution and you'll learn a lot
